title: FAR U1·W1 — Conceptual Framework & the Four Statements (CPA Core · from CMA m1)
lessonHtml:
Cold open — build every statement from one real trial balance

Real MBG facts: the MBG general ledger totals $12,480,000.00 and Riverton totals $16,920,000.00, both balanced. FAR begins where the CMA program began (month 1): the trial balance is the anchor, and every financial statement is derived from it. This CPA Core unit teaches the conceptual framework and the four statements at exam depth, using MBG's real ledger as the worked example.

The FASB conceptual framework

The objective of general-purpose financial reporting is to provide information useful to investors, lenders, and creditors in making decisions about providing resources. Two fundamental qualitative characteristics make information useful: relevance (it can influence decisions — predictive value, confirmatory value, materiality) and faithful representation (complete, neutral, and free from error). Four enhancing characteristics improve usefulness: comparability, verifiability, timeliness, and understandability. The overriding constraint is cost versus benefit.

The framework also defines the elements (assets, liabilities, equity, revenues, expenses, gains, losses), the assumptions (economic entity, going concern, monetary unit, periodicity), and the principles (historical cost, revenue recognition, matching, full disclosure). For MBG, the economic-entity assumption is why MBG and Riverton are never combined on a single statement — each is its own reporting entity.

The four statements and how they articulate

  • Balance sheet (statement of financial position) — assets = liabilities + equity at a point in time. MBG's WIP/construction-in-progress sits here as an asset until a home closes.
  • Income statement — revenues − expenses = net income for a period.
  • Statement of changes in equity — beginning equity + net income + contributions − distributions = ending equity.
  • Statement of cash flows — operating, investing, and financing cash flows reconciling beginning to ending cash.

Articulation ties them together: net income from the income statement flows into the statement of changes in equity, whose ending equity appears on the balance sheet, and the change in cash on the balance sheet equals the bottom line of the cash flow statement. A set of statements that does not articulate is internally inconsistent — the same discipline as keeping MBG's trial balance in balance.

Worked articulation on MBG

Illustrative figures anchored to MBG's scale: beginning equity $4,000,000, net income $988,000 (from the CMA program's illustrative income statement), and owner distributions $300,000. Ending equity = $4,000,000 + $988,000 − $300,000 = $4,688,000, which is the equity figure that must appear on the period-end balance sheet. If the balance sheet showed a different equity number, the statements would not articulate and an error exists to find — exactly the reconciliation mindset the construction close demands.

Recognition and measurement bases

FAR tests multiple measurement bases: historical cost, net realizable value, current/replacement cost, present value, and fair value (ASC 820, introduced in CMA month 7). An item is recognized when it meets an element definition and is measurable. Knowing which basis applies to which account — receivables at net realizable value, most PP&E at historical cost less depreciation, certain investments at fair value — is a recurring FAR exam skill.

CMA bridge

This unit is the FAR counterpart to CMA month 1 (External Financial Reporting). The CMA program taught you to build statements from MBG's real trial balance; FAR adds the authoritative framework, the qualitative characteristics, and the standards-level rigor the CPA exam expects.

Practice and recap

  1. State the objective of financial reporting and the two fundamental qualitative characteristics.
  2. List the four statements and how net income, equity, and cash articulate across them.
  3. Compute ending equity and tie it to the balance sheet.
  4. Match an account to its measurement basis.

Recap: the conceptual framework makes relevance and faithful representation the test of useful information; the four statements articulate so net income, equity, and cash all tie; and MBG's illustrative ending equity of $4,688,000 must reconcile across the set — the trial-balance discipline carried into FAR.

quiz.title: Conceptual Framework and the Four Statements

questions.q: The two FUNDAMENTAL qualitative characteristics of useful financial information are:
questions.explain: Relevance and faithful representation are fundamental; comparability, verifiability, timeliness, and understandability are enhancing.

questions.q: Faithful representation requires information to be:
choices: Complete, neutral, and free from error
questions.explain: Faithful representation is complete, neutral, and free from error.

questions.q: Net income flows directly into which statement before reaching the balance sheet?
questions.explain: Net income increases the statement of changes in equity, whose ending equity appears on the balance sheet.

questions.q: Beginning equity $4,000,000, net income $988,000, distributions $300,000. Ending equity is:
MBG and Riverton are reported separately because of which assumption?
questions.explain: The economic-entity assumption treats each entity as its own reporting unit.

questions.q: Construction-in-progress (WIP) appears on which statement until a home closes?
questions.explain: WIP/CIP is a balance-sheet asset until the home closes and revenue/cost are recognized.

questions.q: Accounts receivable are generally measured at:
questions.explain: Receivables are reported at net realizable value (net of expected uncollectibles).
